question: Do English-language short fiction works of 1820-1853 and of 1886-1892 differ in how often they use the vocabulary of fear, and which words are key in the later works?

corpus.description: Six short stories and novellas in English; one document is one work, the whole text as Project Gutenberg gives it (header, footer and licence removed).
corpus.selection: Project Gutenberg books 41, 932, 11231 (published 1820-1853) and 43, 375, 1952 (published 1886-1892), chosen for the test fixture as well-known works of their decades that are short enough to record.
corpus.sampling: purposive: three canonical works from each period, not a random sample

author.description: first author as in the catalogue

year.source: entered by hand for the test fixture: Irving 1820 (The Sketch Book), Poe 1839 (Burton's Gentleman's Magazine), Melville 1853 (Putnam's Monthly), Stevenson 1886, Bierce 1890 (San Francisco Examiner), Gilman 1892 (The New England Magazine)

stopwords.source: scikit-learn ENGLISH_STOP_WORDS (318 words), written by build_data.py

preprocessing.front_matter: Project Gutenberg's header, footer and licence removed by the connector; titles and the table of contents of Jekyll and Hyde kept (a few hundred tokens)

analyses.note: a key term must occur in at least 2 of the 3 later works, so one work's names and topics do not make the list

dictionary.name: fear vocabulary
dictionary.source: written for this test fixture: words for fear and its expression, not a published dictionary

analyses.note: one work per year, so a year's figure is one work's

analyses.selection: reconstruction error of each k, and reading the top terms and example segments

limits.sampling_bias: Six canonical works chosen by hand, three per period, all out of U.S. copyright and digitised by Project Gutenberg; American authors dominate the early period. The corpus describes these six works, not the fiction of either period.
